title: Template for general-purpose AI model providers to summarise their training content

evidence.quote: All providers of general-purpose AI models are required to publish a summary of the content used to train their models, based on a template provided by the Commission.
The Summary must be made publicly available no later than when a model is placed on the Union market.

The Template provides a uniform baseline for information to be publicly disclosed in the Summary, consisting of three main sections: General information, List of data sources, Relevant data processing aspects.
Non-compliance may result in fines of up to 3% of the provider's annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year, or 15 000 000 Euros, whichever is higher.
Failure to provide this summary can lead to enforcement actions by the AI Office as of 2 August 2026.

policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Template use is mandatory under Article 53(1)(d) of the AI Act. Obligation applies from 2 August 2025 for new models; existing models have until 2 August 2027. Enforcement actions possible from 2 August 2026. Applies to open-source model providers as well. Code of Practice adherence remains voluntary and addresses separate obligations.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document frames AI governance primarily around enabling rights-holders to exercise their legal rights—copyright, data protection, non-discrimination, consumer protection—under Union law. The core justification for the transparency obligation is that parties with legitimate interests need information to assert their rights, not safety or competitiveness concerns.

evidence_spans.quote: This increased transparency enables parties with legitimate interests to exercise their rights under Union law. These may refer to copyright, related rights, and other intellectual property rights, as well as other rights protected under Union law, such as data protection, consumer protection, non-discrimination, and freedom of science.
The transparency of the training data will help rightsholders in obtaining relevant information on the content used in the training of general-purpose AI models.
